question.value: What are the properties, kinematics, and excitation conditions of the submillimeter continuum and molecular gas in the immediate vicinity of the central massive black hole in the dwarf starburst galaxy Henize 2–10, and how do they relate to positive BH feedback?

evidence.quote: Here we present ALMA continuum observations from 99 to 340 GHz, as well as spectral line observations of the molecules CO (1–0, 3–2), HCN (1–0, 3–2), and HCO+ (1–0, 3–2), with a focus on the BH and its vicinity.
Here we present the first study of the molecular gas in the immediate vicinity of the central BH using high-resolution observations with ALMA.

claims.hypothesis: The radio-to-submillimeter (1.4 to 340 GHz) SED of the central BH in He 2–10 is dominated by non-thermal synchrotron emission.
claims.experiment: Convolved ALMA 99, 113, 251, and 340 GHz continuum images to a common 0.55" x 0.32" beam, measured aperture photometry at the 2MASS/LBA-aligned BH position, and fitted 1-, 2-, and 3-component models across 1.4–340 GHz.
claims.result: A single non-thermal power-law model provides the only physical and well-constrained fit: S_nu = (1349 +/- 217) nu^(-0.52 +/- 0.06) uJy.
claims.finding: The spectral energy distribution of the BH is dominated by synchrotron emission from 1.4 to 340 GHz with spectral index alpha approx -0.52.

evidence.quote: Incorporating cm-wave radio measurements from the literature, we show that the spectral energy distribution of the BH is dominated by synchrotron emission from 1.4 to 340 GHz with a spectral index of α ≈− 0 . 5.

evidence.loc: 3.1. Continuum Emission and Radio SED of the Black Hole

claims.hypothesis: The low Eddington accretion rate of the massive BH is linked to the spatial distribution of molecular gas in its immediate vicinity.
claims.experiment: Generated restricted-velocity (852.1–904.6 km s^-1) moment maps of CO (1-0), CO (3-2), and HCO+ (3-2) to isolate the molecular structure around the BH.
claims.result: Identified an elongated molecular structure (128 pc x 34 pc, M_H2 = (0.21–1.53) x 10^6 M_sun) with mean velocity ~880 km s^-1, with the BH located at its northern edge and significantly offset from the peak intensity.
claims.finding: The spatial offset of the BH from the molecular gas peak intensity, likely caused by star formation feedback to the north, can explain why the BH radiates at a very low Eddington ratio.

evidence.quote: Despite an abundance of molecular gas in this general region, the position of the BH is significantly offset from the peak intensity, which may explain why the BH is radiating at a very low Eddington ratio.

claims.hypothesis: The bipolar outflow from the BH shocks and excites the cold molecular gas at the interfaces with surrounding clouds, driving positive BH feedback.
claims.experiment: Computed a beam-matched (0.45" x 0.30") pixel-by-pixel CO (3-2)/(1-0) line ratio map (R_31) and compared it with the HST H-alpha outflow morphology.
claims.result: Measured elevated line ratios at the eastern outflow-starburst interface (R_31 = 2.7 +/- 0.2) and western dark cloud boundary region 5 (R_31 = 2.5 +/- 0.7), compared to R_31 = 1.3 +/- 0.1 in the rest of the BH vicinity.
claims.finding: The cold molecular gas at both ends of the bipolar outflow is highly excited by shock heating and compression from the BH outflow, supporting positive BH feedback.

evidence.quote: Our analysis of the spatially-resolved line ratio between CO J=3–2 and J=1–0 implies that the CO gas in the vicinity of the BH is highly excited, particularly at the interface between the BH outflow and the regions of triggered star formation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Table 2 is completely missing (blank page 5 in the manuscript), omitting key tclean imaging parameters, line-free channel ranges, and cube noise/beam properties.

There are internal inconsistencies in the text vs. conclusions for the western region column density and extinction: Section 3.2.6 reports N(H2) = 2.21e22 to 1.58e23 cm^-2 and A_V ~ 21–152 mag, whereas Section 4 (Conclusions) states N(H2) ~ 10^21-22 cm^-2 and A_V >= 2–11 mag.
The position angle of the BH vicinity ellipse is stated as 80.34 deg in the text (Section 3.2.3) but 83.34 deg in Table 3.

The 340 GHz flux density in region 6 is attributed entirely to thermal dust emission without subtracting potential free-free continuum contribution, despite noting earlier that the central starburst regions are dominated by free-free emission.
